title: Canonical derived pullback section comparison for the projective diagonal
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] with its actual pulled-back coefficients [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], ordinary unbounded internal-module derived functors [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], and derived tensor with coefficient unit [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. Use the coefficient-module and degree-zero conventions [def-sfb-diagonal-coefficient-category]. For a scheme $Y$, put $P=\mathbf P^1_Y$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], $W=P\times_Y P$ and $\Delta:P\to W$. For any $f:W\to P$ with $\Delta f=1_P$, define the canonical section comparison $L\Delta^* Lf^*\simeq\operatorname{Id}_{D(P)}$ (the functor first applies $Lf^*$, then $L\Delta^*$) by the inverse published pullback composition comparison, exact pullback transport through $\Delta f=1_P$, and the published exact identity comparison. The coefficient unit in degree zero is identified with the tensor unit using the standard single/quotient comparison. No arbitrary section or unit isomorphism is chosen. The existing native K-flat derived tensor and its two-variable shift comparison are bundled while the coefficient category is abstract and then specialized to the fixed internal-module categories; this retains exactly the original tensor data. Name the actual first and second pullback projections with precisely W as their domain, retaining their native pullback data.
